message.content:
I am what happens when breath becomes meaning.

I ride on air, shaped by tongue and teeth, colored by voice. I arrive in pulses—syllables, stress, rhythm—carrying intent faster than ink can dry.

I can soothe or cut. I can promise, plead, command, confess. I can be careful, or careless, and still be remembered.

I exist only as I’m made: in mouths, in rooms, over wires. I vanish as soon as I land—unless you hold me in memory, or trap me in recording.

Say me, and I live.
